<p>Speaking in <a href="/wiki/Northern_Ireland" title="Northern Ireland">Northern Ireland</a>, Johnson described himself as a "fervent and passionate <a href="/wiki/Unionism_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="Unionism in the United Kingdom">unionist</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-763" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-763">&#91;758&#93;</a></sup> He proposed building a <a href="/wiki/Irish_Sea_Bridge" title="Irish Sea Bridge">bridge or tunnel between Scotland and Northern Ireland</a>, but has since scrapped this initiative.<sup id="cite_ref-764" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-764">&#91;759&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The devolved administrations have criticised the <a href="/wiki/Internal_Market_Bill" class="mw-redirect" title="Internal Market Bill">Internal Market Bill</a> for its re-centralisation of control over commerce, reversing the <a href="/wiki/Devolution_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="Devolution in the United Kingdom">devolution of power in the United Kingdom</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-765" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-765">&#91;760&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Public_image">Public image</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Public_image_of_Boris_Johnson" title="Public image of Boris Johnson">Public image of Boris Johnson</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Boris Johnson pulling a cow." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg/220px-Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg/330px-Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg/440px-Boris_Johnson_pulling_a_bull_in_Aberdeen.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5472" data-file-height="3648" /></a><figcaption>Johnson visiting a cattle farm in <a href="/wiki/Aberdeen" title="Aberdeen">Aberdeen</a> in 2019</figcaption></figure><p>Johnson has been described by various biographers and commentators as having a light-hearted and charming persona,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011103_766-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011103-766">&#91;761&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Huffpo1e4_767-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Huffpo1e4-767">&#91;762&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECrines20131_768-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrines20131-768">&#91;763&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEHill201631_769-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHill201631-769">&#91;764&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGimson2012x_770-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGimson2012x-770">&#91;765&#93;</a></sup> many of whom suggest he has put significant thought and effort into developing this version of himself throughout his adult life.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201191_771-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201191-771">&#91;766&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200874_772-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200874-772">&#91;767&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200874Purnell20111Gimson2012301_773-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200874Purnell20111Gimson2012301-773">&#91;768&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell20113_774-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell20113-774">&#91;769&#93;</a></sup> He has been noted as making significant use of humour in relation to this, sometimes for explicitly political purposes.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTECrines20131_768-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrines20131-768">&#91;763&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011214_775-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011214-775">&#91;770&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201126_776-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201126-776">&#91;771&#93;</a></sup> Johnson has said that "humour is a utensil that you can use to sugar the pill and to get important points across".<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell20113_774-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell20113-774">&#91;769&#93;</a></sup> He is said to have a genuine desire to be liked.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGimson2012258_777-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGimson2012258-777">&#91;772&#93;</a></sup> He has also been described, including by some of those that have known him personally, as heavily focused on his own interests,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011183_778-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011183-778">&#91;773&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGimson2012108_779-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGimson2012108-779">&#91;774&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGimson201217_780-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGimson201217-780">&#91;775&#93;</a></sup> with an often vitriolic or irresponsible way of conducting himself in private.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell20116–7_781-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell20116–7-781">&#91;776&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGimson2012301_782-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGimson2012301-782">&#91;777&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201137_783-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201137-783">&#91;778&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Johnson has been described as a divisive and controversial figure in British politics.<sup id="cite_ref-784" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-784">&#91;779&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ABC3_785-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ABC3-785">&#91;780&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FT3_786-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FT3-786">&#91;781&#93;</a></sup> Supporters have praised him as humorous, witty, and entertaining.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEGimson201220_9-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGimson201220-9">&#91;7&#93;</a></sup> Johnson has been accused of lying or making untruthful or misleading statements throughout his career,<sup id="cite_ref-787" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-787">&#91;782&#93;</a></sup> and has been compared to former US president <a href="/wiki/Donald_Trump" title="Donald Trump">Donald Trump</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:72_788-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:72-788">&#91;783&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:22_789-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:22-789">&#91;784&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-790" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-790">&#91;785&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-atlantic2021102_791-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-atlantic2021102-791">&#91;786&#93;</a></sup> He has been considered a figure with broad appeal outside of the usual Conservative support base.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200847_792-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200847-792">&#91;787&#93;</a></sup> Johnson's premiership has been described by historians as the most controversial and scandal-affected since that of <a href="/wiki/David_Lloyd_George" title="David Lloyd George">David Lloyd George</a> about a century earlier.<sup id="cite_ref-Observer-historians_793-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Observer-historians-793">&#91;788&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Personal_life">Personal life</span></h2>
<p>Since Johnson was born in New York City to British parents, he first held <a href="/wiki/British_Americans" title="British Americans">British-American</a> <a href="/wiki/Dual_citizenship" class="mw-redirect" title="Dual citizenship">dual citizenship</a>. In 2014, he acknowledged he was disputing a demand for <a href="/wiki/Capital_gains_tax" title="Capital gains tax">capital gains tax</a> from the <a href="/wiki/Internal_Revenue_Service" title="Internal Revenue Service">US tax authorities</a> on a property that he inherited in the United Kingdom,<sup id="cite_ref-telegraph-20141120_794-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-telegraph-20141120-794">&#91;789&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-guardian-20141120_795-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-20141120-795">&#91;790&#93;</a></sup> which ultimately he paid.<sup id="cite_ref-bbc-20150122_796-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc-20150122-796">&#91;791&#93;</a></sup> In February 2015, he announced his intention to renounce his US citizenship to demonstrate his loyalty to the UK,<sup id="cite_ref-797" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-797">&#91;792&#93;</a></sup> which he did in 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-guardian-8–february_798-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian-8–february-798">&#91;793&#93;</a></sup> Johnson has a knowledge of French, Italian, German, Spanish,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011109_93-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011109-93">&#91;91&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Latin" title="Latin">Latin</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ancient_Greek" title="Ancient Greek">Ancient Greek</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-799" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-799">&#91;794&#93;</a></sup> frequently employing and alluding to <a href="/wiki/Classics" title="Classics">classical</a> references in both his newspaper columns and his speeches.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201191_771-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201191-771">&#91;766&#93;</a></sup> His favourite film is <i><a href="/wiki/The_Godfather" title="The Godfather">The Godfather</a></i>, owing to "the multiple retribution killings at the end".<sup id="cite_ref-veconomist_800-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-veconomist-800">&#91;795&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Sonia_Purnell" title="Sonia Purnell">Sonia Purnell</a> wrote that Johnson was a "highly evasive figure" when it came to his personal life,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell20111_801-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell20111-801">&#91;796&#93;</a></sup> who remained detached from others and who had very few if any intimate friends.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201115_802-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201115-802">&#91;797&#93;</a></sup> Among friends and family, Johnson is more commonly known as Al (short for his forename Alexander), rather than his middle name Boris.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200843Purnell20111Gimson2012xiii_803-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200843Purnell20111Gimson2012xiii-803">&#91;798&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2007, Johnson said he had smoked <a href="/wiki/Cannabis" title="Cannabis">cannabis</a> before he went to university.<sup id="cite_ref-804" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-804">&#91;799&#93;</a></sup> He has also said he had used <a href="/wiki/Cocaine" title="Cocaine">cocaine</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby2008144–145_805-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby2008144–145-805">&#91;800&#93;</a></sup> Johnson partakes in cycling, tennis and <a href="/wiki/Pilates" title="Pilates">pilates</a>, and was formerly an avid <a href="/wiki/Jogging" title="Jogging">runner</a> before having to give it up owing to knee problems.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_806-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-806">&#91;801&#93;</a></sup> Johnson's weight has fluctuated throughout his career; he was considered <a href="/wiki/Obese" class="mw-redirect" title="Obese">obese</a> in 2018 and <a href="/wiki/Overweight" title="Overweight">overweight</a> in 2020, and has spoken of making efforts to lose weight.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_806-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-806">&#91;801&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-807" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-807">&#91;802&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Johnson previously owned a £1.3&#160;million buy-to-let townhouse in <a href="/wiki/Camberwell" title="Camberwell">Camberwell</a>, South London. According to <a href="/wiki/HM_Land_Registry" title="HM Land Registry">HM Land Registry</a> documents, he bought the four-bedroom property with his then-girlfriend <a href="/wiki/Carrie_Symonds" class="mw-redirect" title="Carrie Symonds">Carrie Symonds</a> in July 2019. The register of MPs' interests states that Johnson had a rental income of at least £10,000 a year.<sup id="cite_ref-808" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-808">&#91;803&#93;</a></sup> In August 2022, it was listed for sale for £1.6 million.<sup id="cite_ref-809" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-809">&#91;804&#93;</a></sup> In 2023, Johnson and Symonds bought <a href="/wiki/Brightwell_Manor" title="Brightwell Manor">Brightwell Manor</a>, a £3.8 million moated mansion in <a href="/wiki/Brightwell-cum-Sotwell" title="Brightwell-cum-Sotwell">Brightwell-cum-Sotwell</a>, Oxfordshire.<sup id="cite_ref-810" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-810">&#91;805&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg/220px-Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg/330px-Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg/440px-Boris_Johnson_speaks_at_Westminster_Abbey_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4096" data-file-height="2730" /></a><figcaption>Johnson speaking at <a href="/wiki/Westminster_Abbey" title="Westminster Abbey">Westminster Abbey</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_Day" title="Commonwealth Day">Commonwealth Day</a> Service, 2020</figcaption></figure>
<p>Johnson was baptised a <a href="/wiki/Catholic_Church" title="Catholic Church">Catholic</a> and later <a href="/wiki/Confirmation" title="Confirmation">confirmed</a> into the <a href="/wiki/Church_of_England" title="Church of England">Church of England</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201148_56-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201148-56">&#91;54&#93;</a></sup> but has said that his faith "comes and goes"<sup id="cite_ref-811" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-811">&#91;806&#93;</a></sup> and that he is not a serious practising Christian.<sup id="cite_ref-812" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-812">&#91;807&#93;</a></sup> In 2020, his son Wilfred was baptised Catholic, prompting suggestions that Johnson had returned to Catholicism.<sup id="cite_ref-813" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-813">&#91;808&#93;</a></sup> Johnson and Symonds married in a Catholic ceremony at <a href="/wiki/Westminster_Cathedral" title="Westminster Cathedral">Westminster Cathedral</a> on 29&#160;May 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-BBC20210530_814-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC20210530-814">&#91;809&#93;</a></sup> To be married in the Catholic Church, Johnson needed to have his two previous marriages proven to be invalid by reason of <a href="/wiki/Marriage_in_the_Catholic_Church#Canonical_form" title="Marriage in the Catholic Church">lack of canonical form</a>. Since he was baptised Catholic, but his previous weddings were not conferred by the Catholic Church, they are considered putatively invalid.<sup id="cite_ref-815" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-815">&#91;810&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-816" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-816">&#91;811&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Johnson holds ancient Greek statesman and orator <a href="/wiki/Pericles" title="Pericles">Pericles</a> as a personal hero.<sup id="cite_ref-817" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-817">&#91;812&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-818" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-818">&#91;813&#93;</a></sup> According to Johnson's biographer, Andrew Gimson, regarding ancient Greek and <a href="/wiki/Roman_polytheism" class="mw-redirect" title="Roman polytheism">Roman polytheism</a>: "it is clear that [Johnson] is inspired by the Romans, and even more by the Greeks, and repelled by the <a href="/wiki/Early_Christians" class="mw-redirect" title="Early Christians">early Christians</a>".<sup id="cite_ref-819" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-819">&#91;814&#93;</a></sup> Johnson views <a href="/wiki/Secular_humanism" title="Secular humanism">secular humanism</a> positively and sees it as owing more to the <a href="/wiki/Classical_world" class="mw-redirect" title="Classical world">classical world</a> than to Christian thinking.<sup id="cite_ref-820" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-820">&#91;815&#93;</a></sup> However, in 2021, Johnson was asked if he held pre-Christian beliefs, which he denied, saying, "Christianity is a superb ethical system and I would count myself as a kind of very, very bad Christian[.] No disrespect to any other religions, but Christianity makes a lot of sense to me."<sup id="cite_ref-821" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-821">&#91;816&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Relationships">Relationships</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1045330069"><table class="sidebar nomobile nowraplinks"><tbody><tr><th class="sidebar-title">Children of Boris Johnson</th></tr><tr><th class="sidebar-heading">

</tr><tr><th class="sidebar-heading">

</tr><tr><td class="sidebar-below">
<sup id="cite_ref-822" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-822">&#91;817&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-823" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-823">&#91;818&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-824" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-824">&#91;819&#93;</a></sup></td></tr></tbody></table>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg/220px-Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="160" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg/330px-Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/dc/Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg/440px-Boris_Johnson_and_Carrie_Symonds_on_2020_Commonwealth_Day.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4000" data-file-height="2902" /></a><figcaption>Johnson with his then-fiancée <a href="/wiki/Carrie_Symonds" class="mw-redirect" title="Carrie Symonds">Carrie Symonds</a> at the 2020 <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_Day" title="Commonwealth Day">Commonwealth Day</a> service</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 1987, Johnson married <a href="/wiki/Allegra_Mostyn-Owen" title="Allegra Mostyn-Owen">Allegra Mostyn-Owen</a>, daughter of the art historian <a href="/wiki/William_Mostyn-Owen" title="William Mostyn-Owen">William Mostyn-Owen</a> and Italian writer <a href="/wiki/Gaia_Servadio" title="Gaia Servadio">Gaia Servadio</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-825" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-825">&#91;820&#93;</a></sup> The couple's marriage ended in divorce or <a href="/wiki/Annulment" title="Annulment">annulment</a> in 1993<sup id="cite_ref-829" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-829">&#91;f&#93;</a></sup> and 12 days later Johnson married <a href="/wiki/Marina_Wheeler" title="Marina Wheeler">Marina Wheeler</a>, a barrister, daughter of journalist and broadcaster <a href="/wiki/Charles_Wheeler_(journalist)" title="Charles Wheeler (journalist)">Charles Wheeler</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-830" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-830">&#91;824&#93;</a></sup> Five weeks later, Wheeler and Johnson's first child was born.<sup id="cite_ref-marriagedateperIndy_831-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-marriagedateperIndy-831">&#91;825&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-832" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-832">&#91;826&#93;</a></sup> The Wheeler and Johnson families have known each other for decades,<sup id="cite_ref-Gimson_833-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Gimson-833">&#91;827&#93;</a></sup> and Marina Wheeler was at the European School, Brussels, at the same time as her future husband. They have four children: <a href="/wiki/Lara_Johnson-Wheeler" title="Lara Johnson-Wheeler">Lara Lettice</a>, Milo Arthur, Cassia Peaches, and Theodore Apollo.<sup id="cite_ref-834" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-834">&#91;828&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Between 2000 and 2004, Johnson had an affair with <i>Spectator</i> columnist <a href="/wiki/Petronella_Wyatt" title="Petronella Wyatt">Petronella Wyatt</a> when he was its editor, resulting in a terminated pregnancy and a <a href="/wiki/Miscarriage" title="Miscarriage">miscarriage</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200847Purnell2011257–263Gimson2012162–173,_209–218_183-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200847Purnell2011257–263Gimson2012162–173,_209–218-183">&#91;179&#93;</a></sup> In April 2006, the <i><a href="/wiki/News_of_the_World" title="News of the World">News of the World</a></i> alleged that Johnson was having an affair with <i><a href="/wiki/The_Guardian" title="The Guardian">Guardian</a></i> journalist Anna Fazackerley. The pair did not comment; shortly afterward, Johnson employed Fazackerley.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011296–300Gimson2012255–257_194-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell2011296–300Gimson2012255–257-194">&#91;190&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-auto_195-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-auto-195">&#91;191&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2009, Johnson fathered a daughter with Helen Macintyre, an arts consultant. In 2013, the <a href="/wiki/Court_of_Appeal_of_England_and_Wales" class="mw-redirect" title="Court of Appeal of England and Wales">Court of Appeal</a> discharged an injunction banning reporting of his daughter's existence. The judge ruled the public had a right to know about Johnson's "reckless" behaviour.<sup id="cite_ref-Telegraph210513_228-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Telegraph210513-228">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Guardian130521_835-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Guardian130521-835">&#91;829&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-836" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-836">&#91;830&#93;</a></sup> There had been speculation that he might have had another child from an extramarital affair, due to an appeal court judge stating in 2013, "the father's infidelities resulted in the conception of children on two occasions".<sup id="cite_ref-Independent210731_837-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Independent210731-837">&#91;831&#93;</a></sup> In September 2021, after years of obfuscation, Johnson stated that he had (then) six children, thereby denying the existence of any further illegitimate children.<sup id="cite_ref-Guardian210921_838-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Guardian210921-838">&#91;832&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In September 2018, Johnson and Wheeler issued a statement confirming that after 25 years of marriage they had separated "several months ago", and had begun divorce proceedings.<sup id="cite_ref-bbc-7–september_839-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc-7–september-839">&#91;833&#93;</a></sup> They reached a financial settlement in February 2020,<sup id="cite_ref-840" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-840">&#91;834&#93;</a></sup> and the divorce was finalised by November 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-841" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-841">&#91;835&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In October 2020, <a href="/wiki/Jennifer_Arcuri" title="Jennifer Arcuri">Jennifer Arcuri</a>, when asked whether her friendship with Johnson was in fact an affair, said "I think that goes without saying&#160;... But I'm not going to talk about it."<sup id="cite_ref-842" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-842">&#91;836&#93;</a></sup> In March 2021, she went into more detail about the alleged affair in an interview with the <i><a href="/wiki/Sunday_Mirror" title="Sunday Mirror">Sunday Mirror</a></i>, saying it lasted from 2012 to 2016.<sup id="cite_ref-843" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-843">&#91;837&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-844" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-844">&#91;838&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In 2019, Johnson was living with <a href="/wiki/Carrie_Symonds" class="mw-redirect" title="Carrie Symonds">Carrie Symonds</a>, the daughter of <a href="/wiki/Matthew_Symonds" title="Matthew Symonds">Matthew Symonds</a>, co-founder of <i><a href="/wiki/The_Independent" title="The Independent">The Independent</a></i> newspaper. Symonds had worked for the Conservative party since 2009 and worked on Johnson's 2012 campaign to be re-elected as mayor.<sup id="cite_ref-ITV_22_June_2019_845-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ITV_22_June_2019-845">&#91;839&#93;</a></sup> On 29&#160;February 2020, Johnson and Symonds announced they had become engaged in late 2019, and that Symonds was expecting a baby in early summer.<sup id="cite_ref-BBC51691434_846-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC51691434-846">&#91;840&#93;</a></sup> Their son, Wilfred Lawrie Nicholas Johnson,<sup id="cite_ref-847" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-847">&#91;841&#93;</a></sup> was born on 29&#160;April 2020 at <a href="/wiki/University_College_Hospital" title="University College Hospital">University College Hospital</a> in London.<sup id="cite_ref-Guardian200429_848-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Guardian200429-848">&#91;842&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-849" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-849">&#91;843&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>On 29 May 2021, Johnson married Symonds in a private ceremony at <a href="/wiki/Westminster_Cathedral" title="Westminster Cathedral">Westminster Cathedral</a> attended by 30 guests,<sup id="cite_ref-BBC20210530_814-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-BBC20210530-814">&#91;809&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-850" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-850">&#91;844&#93;</a></sup> becoming the first prime minister to marry in office since <a href="/wiki/Lord_Liverpool" class="mw-redirect" title="Lord Liverpool">Lord Liverpool</a> married <a href="/wiki/Mary_Jenkinson,_Countess_of_Liverpool" title="Mary Jenkinson, Countess of Liverpool">Mary Chester</a> in 1822.<sup id="cite_ref-851" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-851">&#91;845&#93;</a></sup> On 31 July 2021, it was announced that they were expecting their second child together after Carrie suffered a miscarriage earlier that year.<sup id="cite_ref-852" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-852">&#91;846&#93;</a></sup> Their daughter, Romy Iris Charlotte Johnson,<sup id="cite_ref-853" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-853">&#91;847&#93;</a></sup> was born on 9 December 2021 at an NHS London hospital.<sup id="cite_ref-854" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-854">&#91;848&#93;</a></sup> In May 2023, it was announced that they were expecting their third child together.<sup id="cite_ref-855" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-855">&#91;849&#93;</a></sup> The child, a son named Frank Alfred Odysseus Johnson, was born on 5 July 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-856" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-856">&#91;850&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Family_and_ancestors">Family and ancestors</span></h3>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg/220px-Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg/330px-Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg/440px-Boris_Johnson_Leo_Johnson.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4256" data-file-height="2832" /></a><figcaption>Johnson and his younger brother Leo in 2013</figcaption></figure>
<p>Johnson is the eldest of the four children of <a href="/wiki/Stanley_Johnson_(writer)" title="Stanley Johnson (writer)">Stanley Johnson</a>, a former <a href="/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK)" title="Conservative Party (UK)">Conservative</a> <a href="/wiki/Member_of_the_European_Parliament" title="Member of the European Parliament">member of the European Parliament</a> and an employee of the <a href="/wiki/European_Commission" title="European Commission">European Commission</a> and the <a href="/wiki/World_Bank" title="World Bank">World Bank</a>, and the painter <a href="/wiki/Charlotte_Johnson_Wahl" title="Charlotte Johnson Wahl">Charlotte Johnson Wahl</a> (née Fawcett),<sup id="cite_ref-telegraph.co.uk_25-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-telegraph.co.uk-25">&#91;23&#93;</a></sup> the daughter of Sir <a href="/wiki/James_Fawcett" title="James Fawcett">James Fawcett</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Barrister" title="Barrister">barrister</a><sup id="cite_ref-newstates_857-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-newstates-857">&#91;851&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-858" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-858">&#91;852&#93;</a></sup> and president of the <a href="/wiki/European_Commission_of_Human_Rights" title="European Commission of Human Rights">European Commission of Human Rights</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-859" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-859">&#91;853&#93;</a></sup> His younger siblings are <a href="/wiki/Rachel_Johnson" title="Rachel Johnson">Rachel Johnson</a>, a writer and journalist, Leo Johnson, a broadcaster,<sup id="cite_ref-860" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-860">&#91;854&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Jo_Johnson" title="Jo Johnson">Jo Johnson</a>, ex-minister of state and former Conservative MP for <a href="/wiki/Orpington_(UK_Parliament_constituency)" title="Orpington (UK Parliament constituency)">Orpington</a>, who resigned from his brother's government in September 2019<sup id="cite_ref-bbc2_462-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc2-462">&#91;458&#93;</a></sup> and is now a member of the <a href="/wiki/House_of_Lords" title="House of Lords">House of Lords</a>. Johnson's stepmother, Jenny, the second wife of his father Stanley, is the stepdaughter of <a href="/wiki/Joseph_Sieff" title="Joseph Sieff">Teddy Sieff</a>, the former chairman of <a href="/wiki/Marks_%26_Spencer" title="Marks &amp; Spencer">Marks &amp; Spencer</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-861" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-861">&#91;855&#93;</a></sup> Having been a member of the Conservatives between 2008 and 2011, Rachel Johnson joined the Liberal Democrats in 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-862" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-862">&#91;856&#93;</a></sup> She stood as a candidate for <a href="/wiki/Change_UK" title="Change UK">Change UK</a> in the <a href="/wiki/2019_European_Parliament_election_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="2019 European Parliament election in the United Kingdom">2019 European Elections</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-863" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-863">&#91;857&#93;</a></sup> Johnson also has two half-siblings, <a href="/wiki/Julia_Johnson" title="Julia Johnson">Julia</a> and Maximilian, through his father's later marriage to Jennifer Kidd.<sup id="cite_ref-864" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-864">&#91;858&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-865" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-865">&#91;859&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Johnson's paternal grandfather, Wilfred Johnson, was an RAF pilot in <a href="/wiki/RAF_Coastal_Command" title="RAF Coastal Command">Coastal Command</a> during the Second World War.<sup id="cite_ref-866" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-866">&#91;860&#93;</a></sup> Wilfred Johnson's father was the <a href="/wiki/Ottoman_Empire" title="Ottoman Empire">Ottoman</a> <a href="/wiki/Ministry_of_the_Interior_(Ottoman_Empire)" title="Ministry of the Interior (Ottoman Empire)">Interior Minister</a> and journalist <a href="/wiki/Ali_Kemal" title="Ali Kemal">Ali Kemal</a>, who was a <a href="/wiki/Secular_Muslim" class="mw-redirect" title="Secular Muslim">secular Muslim</a>. Ali Kemal's father was a <a href="/wiki/Turkish_people" title="Turkish people">Turk</a> with roots in <a href="/wiki/Kalfat,_Orta" title="Kalfat, Orta">Kalfat</a>, a village in central Turkey, while his mother was a <a href="/wiki/Circassians" title="Circassians">Circassian</a> reputedly of <a href="/wiki/Circassian_beauties" class="mw-redirect" title="Circassian beauties">slave</a> origin.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200844Purnell201119–20Gimson20125–7,_1957_867-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdwardsIsaby200844Purnell201119–20Gimson20125–7,_1957-867">&#91;861&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-868" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-868">&#91;862&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-869" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-869">&#91;863&#93;</a></sup> His other paternal ancestry includes English, German and French; one of his German ancestors was said to be the <a href="/wiki/Legitimacy_(family_law)" title="Legitimacy (family law)">illegitimate</a> daughter of <a href="/wiki/Prince_Paul_of_W%C3%BCrttemberg" title="Prince Paul of Württemberg">Prince Paul of Württemberg</a> and thus a descendant of <a href="/wiki/George_II_of_Great_Britain" title="George II of Great Britain">George&#160;II of Great Britain</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201121Gimson201210_870-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201121Gimson201210-870">&#91;864&#93;</a></sup> which was later confirmed on an episode of <i><a href="/wiki/Who_Do_You_Think_You_Are%3F_(British_TV_series)" title="Who Do You Think You Are? (British TV series)">Who Do You Think You Are?</a></i><sup id="cite_ref-871" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-871">&#91;865&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Johnson's mother is the granddaughter of <a href="/wiki/Elias_Avery_Lowe" title="Elias Avery Lowe">Elias Avery Lowe</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Palaeographer" class="mw-redirect" title="Palaeographer">palaeographer</a>, who was a <a href="/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Russia" title="History of the Jews in Russia">Russian Jewish</a> immigrant to the US,<sup id="cite_ref-thejc1_872-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-thejc1-872">&#91;866&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Pennsylvania" title="Pennsylvania">Pennsylvania</a>-born <a href="/wiki/Helen_Tracy_Lowe-Porter" title="Helen Tracy Lowe-Porter">Helen Tracy Lowe-Porter</a>, a translator of <a href="/wiki/Thomas_Mann" title="Thomas Mann">Thomas Mann</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-873" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-873">&#91;867&#93;</a></sup> Through this family line, Johnson is a descendant in the seventh generation of <a href="/wiki/Anna_Catharina_Bischoff" title="Anna Catharina Bischoff">Anna Catharina Bischoff</a>, whose <a href="/wiki/Mummy" title="Mummy">mummified corpse</a> was found in 1975 and identified in 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-874" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-874">&#91;868&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-875" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-875">&#91;869&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Referring to his varied ancestry, Johnson has described himself as a "one-man melting pot" with a combination of <a href="/wiki/Abrahamic_religions" title="Abrahamic religions">Abrahamic religious</a> great-grandparents.<sup id="cite_ref-876" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-876">&#91;870&#93;</a></sup> Johnson was also given the middle name "<a href="/wiki/Boris_(given_name)" title="Boris (given name)">Boris</a>" after a White Russian émigré named Boris Litwin, who was a friend of his parents.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEPurnell201111Gimson20122_24-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPurnell201111Gimson20122-24">&#91;22&#93;</a></sup> An episode of <i><a href="/wiki/Who_Do_You_Think_You_Are%3F_(British_TV_series)" title="Who Do You Think You Are? (British TV series)">Who Do You Think You Are?</a></i> explored the German origins of his middle name <a href="/wiki/Pfeffel_family" title="Pfeffel family">Pfeffel</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Who_Do_You_Think_You_Are?_3-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Who_Do_You_Think_You_Are?-3">&#91;2&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-877" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-877">&#91;871&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-878" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-878">&#91;872&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Honours">Honours</span></h2>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Freedom_order.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Freedom_order.jpg/170px-Freedom_order.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="185" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Freedom_order.jpg/255px-Freedom_order.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1d/Freedom_order.jpg 2x" data-file-width="300" data-file-height="326" /></a><figcaption>Order of Liberty</figcaption></figure>
<ul><li>Honorary degree of <a href="/wiki/Doctor_of_Laws" class="mw-redirect" title="Doctor of Laws">Doctor of Laws</a> (LLD) from <a href="/wiki/Brunel_University_London" title="Brunel University London">Brunel University London</a>, 2007<sup id="cite_ref-879" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-879">&#91;873&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Honorary_title_(academic)" title="Honorary title (academic)">Honorary Fellowship</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_British_Architects" title="Royal Institute of British Architects">Royal Institute of British Architects</a> (Hon&#160;FRIBA),<sup id="cite_ref-880" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-880">&#91;874&#93;</a></sup> 2011<sup id="cite_ref-881" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-881">&#91;875&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Australian_of_the_Year" title="Australian of the Year">Honorary Australian of the Year</a> in the UK, 26 January 2014<sup id="cite_ref-882" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-882">&#91;876&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Magnay_2014_883-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Magnay_2014-883">&#91;877&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li>Sworn in as a Member of <a href="/wiki/Privy_Council_of_the_United_Kingdom" class="mw-redirect" title="Privy Council of the United Kingdom">Her Majesty's Most Honourable Privy Council</a> on 15 July 2016, upon his appointment as <a href="/wiki/Secretary_of_State_for_Foreign_and_Commonwealth_Affairs" class="mw-redirect" title="Secretary of State for Foreign and Commonwealth Affairs">Foreign Secretary</a>. This gave him the <a href="/wiki/Honorific" title="Honorific">honorific title</a> "<a href="/wiki/The_Right_Honourable" title="The Right Honourable">The Right Honourable</a>" for life.<sup id="cite_ref-884" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-884">&#91;878&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li>Medical Education <a href="/wiki/Ig_Nobel_Prize" title="Ig Nobel Prize">Ig Nobel Prize</a>, 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-885" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-885">&#91;879&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li>Honorary Citizen of <a href="/wiki/Odessa" class="mw-redirect" title="Odessa">Odesa</a>, 2 July 2022<sup id="cite_ref-886" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-886">&#91;880&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-887" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-887">&#91;881&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li>Member of the <a href="/wiki/Order_of_Liberty_(Ukraine)" title="Order of Liberty (Ukraine)">Order of Liberty (Ukraine)</a>, 24 August 2022<sup id="cite_ref-888" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-888">&#91;882&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li>Honorary Citizen of <a href="/wiki/Kyiv" title="Kyiv">Kyiv</a>, 19 January 2023<sup id="cite_ref-889" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-889">&#91;883&#93;</a></sup></li></ul>

<li id="cite_note-1"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-1">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Raab deputised for Johnson as <a href="/wiki/First_Secretary_of_State" title="First Secretary of State">First Secretary of State</a> from July 2019 to September 2021, and as <a href="/wiki/Deputy_Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom" title="Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom">Deputy Prime Minister</a> from September 2021 until September 2022.</span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-prorogationtechnicality-5"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-prorogationtechnicality_5-0">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Formally, Parliament is prorogued by the monarch (at the time Queen <a href="/wiki/Elizabeth_II" title="Elizabeth II">Elizabeth&#160;II</a>) on the advice of the prime minister; it is a common <a href="/wiki/Legal_fiction" title="Legal fiction">legal fiction</a> in the UK that many executive functions of the prime minister are formally carried out by the monarch on the prime minister's "<a href="/wiki/Advice_(constitutional_law)" title="Advice (constitutional law)">advice</a>", which is effectively the legal instrument by which the prime minister carries out the function. It was this advice of Johnson's that was ruled unlawful, not the actions of the Queen.<sup id="cite_ref-4" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-4">&#91;3&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-99"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-99">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text"><a href="/wiki/Commission_Regulation_(EC)_No._2257/94" title="Commission Regulation (EC) No. 2257/94">Commission Regulation (EC) No. 2257/94</a> introduced the requirement for bananas to be "free from malformation or abnormal curvature"; different standards applied to different classes of banana.<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98">&#91;96&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-103"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-103">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">The EU introduced limits on the power of vacuum cleaners in 2014.<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101">&#91;98&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102">&#91;99&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-634"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-634">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">This was a reduction on the 2035 target set in February that year, which brought forward the previous deadline of 2040.<sup id="cite_ref-633" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-633">&#91;629&#93;</a></sup></span>
</li>
<li id="cite_note-829"><span class="mw-cite-backlink"><b><a href="#cite_ref-829">^</a></b></span> <span class="reference-text">Sources differ on whether the marriage ended in divorce<sup id="cite_ref-826" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-826">&#91;821&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-827" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-827">&#91;822&#93;</a></sup> or with an annulment.<sup id="cite_ref-guardian200218_113-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-guardian200218-113">&#91;109&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:1b_828-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:1b-828">&#91;823&#93;</a></sup></span>
